verdicts.reason: Two SETS OF SEARCH ENTRIES in one table, matched on shape alone: the matcher ignores field names, so it sees `panelId`/`topic`/`titleKey`/`descriptionKey`/`keywordsKey` repeated once per setting, which is what a data table is. Consolidating them would mean a builder function that takes seven positional arguments per row, and the whole point of this file is that a row is readable beside the setting it describes (myne-md/myne#1077).

A normalised-skeleton false positive, and the three anchors show it: they land at 2041, 2063 and 2365, which is a record builder, its wrapper and the opening of a test, so the match spans function boundaries rather than describing one body. What the skeleton sees is the order of a few `let`s, a call and a `collect` in short test-support functions that are a fixture, the fixture's caller and a test. Merging any two of them would be wrong: one builds data, one names the shape a test needs, and the third asserts. Recorded so the ratchet keeps its baseline without licensing a copy that exists.

Two TEST BODIES in one file, matched on skeleton: build a `Source` fixture, call one verb, assert on the answer. The normaliser drops the fixture's data and the assertion's expectation, which are the whole of each test: one proves a hit whose note vanished is dropped from a search, the other proves an unknown note id is a different refusal from an out-of-scope one. Factoring the shared shape into a helper would hide which verb each test drives, which is the one thing a reader of a tool-surface test needs to see (myne-md/myne#1077).

The two sheets draw the same header, checkbox row, group separator and Done bar, and they shared that skeleton with SortSheet until the note-list sort was deleted (owner, 2026-11-10) — deleting one copy is what turned a trio into this pair. Consolidating them is owed work and its own change; the entry exists so the ratchet records the pair rather than licensing a further copy of it.

The two 40-line windows the detector pairs are not the same fragment: the AgentHubList window is the conversation-title state machine (one `case` per outcome, each setting its own notice) and the ChatHistoryModal window is the error/loading/empty trio of `<EmptyState>`s. They read as one skeleton only after the vocabulary pass because both now call the same `common.*` keys and the same `setState` shape. Extracting a component would need the title machine and three empty states under one interface, whose only shared part is i18n keys, and that hides which outcome sets which notice. myne-md/myne#1049 review pass.

A normalised-skeleton false positive across seven PrefsView fixture literals: the matcher ignores field names, so it sees the same shape repeated once per test that needs a populated view. The fixtures deliberately spell out every member (no `..Default::default()`) so a new prefs member fails to compile until each test's expectation is decided, which is the compile-time drift lock the sync classification relies on. Consolidating them into one builder would restore the silent default the lock exists to prevent (myne-md/myne#1074).
